chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the two circumcisions meet, it obligates the dower, and the waiting period, and the washing.

key_terms.الْخِتَانَانِ: The two circumcised parts (penis and vagina), referring to sexual intercourse
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period a woman observes after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: The ritual full-body bath required for major ritual purity
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: The dower or bridal gift given to the wife

ai.seo_question: What are the legal obligations that become mandatory upon sexual intercourse in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi defines the physical threshold of consummation as the meeting of the circumcised parts, triggering the obligation of the full dower (mahr al-mithl) and the ritual bath (ghusl). This ruling is pivotal for determining financial rights upon divorce or death, as it distinguishes between partial and complete possession (qabd). The emphasis on ghusl highlights the state of major ritual impurity (janabah) incurred by this specific act, requiring purification before prayer.
